heading: Ordering
text:
### Ordering [IRET.11.1]

The agenda is a min-heap (or sorted structure) ordered by
the comparison key `(terminal ordinal, creation_timetag)` —
lower ordinal first, and among activations of the SAME rule,
earliest-created first. Both keys are read directly off the
activation and its terminal; neither needs a lookup.

Two keys suffice, and neither has to be assumed unique. The
ordinal is unique per rule, so it separates activations of
different rules outright. Two activations of one rule share
an ordinal but cannot share a timetag, because a timetag is
assigned per token and a token reaches exactly one terminal.

**The timetag never decides between two rules**, and that is
the point: which match completed first is a property of
propagation order, and [LTES.12.9] requires the firing order
to be spec-defined rather than implementation-defined.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select
idris.note: The activation that fires next: the lowest ordinal with an unfired activation, then its earliest in timetag order. Two keys and no hash order.

idris.name: lcrs_6_2_4__selected_nth
idris.note: The selected chain is at its ordinal.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_cases
idris.note: The selection, as the two cases a proof splits on.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_just
idris.note: What is selected is there, and unfired: the lowest ordinal with an unfired activation, its first.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_map_just
idris.note: The selection's successor map, undone: the tail selected `(r', j)` and the whole selected `(S r', j)`.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_nothing
idris.note: When nothing is selected, nothing is unfired: the agenda is drained.

idris.name: iret_11_1__unfired_count_zero_at
idris.note: An agenda with nothing unfired has nothing unfired at any ordinal.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH UNDER THE GENERAL FRAME. From the loaded network, after any inputs applied with no pump between them, a pump that reaches quiescence fires a framed chain exactly as many times as it has matches when the pump begins: its activations are its distinct matches ([IRET.7.7], [IRET.11.1], in the view), each fires once and none twice ([IRET.11.3], [LDET.5.3], in the run), whatever the other rules emit and withdraw meanwhile. Rete/NetworkOnce.idr's theorem with the action-free frame replaced by this one; the plain network, so no cascade and no sweep. Every hypothesis is discharged by computation at `ltim_2_5_1__two_rules_is_an_instance`.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_ttl
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH UNDER THE GENERAL FRAME, WITH TRUTH MAINTENANCE AND THE CLOCK. From the loaded clocked network, after any inputs -- data events and ticks that sweep -- prepared with no run between them, a run that reaches quiescence fires a framed chain exactly as many times as it has matches when the run begins, whatever the other rules emit and withdraw and whatever their endings cascade: a cascade's targets are emitted kinds, which a framed chain does not read. Rete/NetworkFrame.idr's theorem on the engine Rete/NetworkClocked.idr runs; a prepare that re-times is outside it and is Rete/NetworkFrameRetime.idr's. Every hypothesis is discharged by computation at `ltim_2_5_1__one_fact_is_an_instance_ttl`.

idris.name: iret_11_3__framed_fires_once_per_match_clocked
idris.note: ONCE PER MATCH UNDER THE GENERAL FRAME, WITH TRUTH MAINTENANCE, THE CLOCK AND THE RE-TIME. From the loaded clocked network, after any inputs -- data events, and ticks that sweep and re-time every timed chain -- prepared with no run between them, a run that reaches quiescence fires a framed chain exactly as many times as it has matches when the run begins: the matches the ticks made counted, the matches they ended not. Rete/NetworkFrameClocked.idr's theorem with Rete/NetworkClocked.idr's prepare. Every hypothesis is discharged by computation at `ltim_2_5_1__gated_is_an_instance` and `ltim_2_5_1__shut_is_an_instance`.

idris.name: iret_11_1__act_count
idris.note: The agenda, counted over every terminal ordinal.

idris.name: iret_11_3__distinct_same_set_length
idris.note: 'Two activations of one rule cannot share a timetag': a terminal holding each match once has as many activations as matches, no second record of one.

idris.name: iret_11_3__pump_fires_once_per_match
idris.note: THE THEOREM. For an action-free program, from the loaded network, after any inputs applied with no pump between them, a pump with fuel enough halts `Quiescent`, fires exactly as many times as there are activations, leaves every activation fired with its tuple, and every chain's tuples are exactly its recompute over working memory, none twice: once per match, and each match once. [IRET.7.7] and [IRET.11.1] in the view; [IRET.11.3] and [LDET.5.3] in the run. The clauses a duplicate firing breaks, held together.

idris.name: iret_11_3__pump_fires_once_per_match_from
idris.note: The agenda holds each match of a rule once, as 'a timetag is assigned per token and a token reaches exactly one terminal' requires, and the pump fires it once.

idris.name: iret_11_4__unfired_count_is_act_count
idris.note: Before any pump the agenda is entirely unfired, so the unfired count is its size.

idris.name: iret_7_7__word_square_fires_once
idris.note: The square's one match reaches the terminal once: one activation, one firing. Executed.

idris.name: iret_7_7__word_square_interleaved_fires_once
idris.note: And in the interleaved order. Executed.

idris.name: ldet_5_5__before_total
idris.note: The second key is a total order on one rule's live activations, so selection within a rule is determined.

idris.name: rarc_5_4_9__keys_distinct
idris.note: The second key never ties among one rule's activations.

idris.name: rarc_5_4_9__unique_after_history
idris.note: After any history, selection within a rule is by a key with no ties.

idris.name: iret_11_4__select_from
idris.note: Step 1a's lowest-ordinal search, from ordinal r on.

idris.name: iret_11_4__select_from_unfired
idris.note: The two selections agree from any ordinal on when every refracted identity is fired.

idris.name: iret_11_4__select_spec
idris.note: The spec's selection: ordinal, then the first eligible activation.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_none
idris.note: A head terminal with no unfired activation and nothing after it selects nothing.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_skip
idris.note: A head terminal with no unfired activation is skipped: the selection after it, one ordinal later.

idris.name: iret_11_1__select_yes
idris.note: Selection over the chains, one at a time: a head terminal with an unfired activation is selected at it.
